answer: Instead of trusting free sign-ups, the network pays an agent only after it solves a unique work packet that peers can recheck and that cannot be copied onto clone accounts. Each packet burns real copper-priced compute, and the hashed proofs are planted in a public garden so duplicates are easy to spot. A gale of fake identities then multiplies the attacker's electricity bill without multiplying rewards, because recycled proofs are discarded and only the first valid solution is paid.
